checker.scope_limitation: the f-in-[G,G] half of the CHARMING predicate is NOT independently recomputed from raw permutations end-to-end (would require normal-closure or abelianization computation on a group of order up to millions, infeasible in pure-Python-stdlib without a permutation-group library, and importing one would violate the standard-library-only rule). The checker instead (a) trusts the producer's charming boolean but (b) independently verifies the SHORT-CIRCUIT STRUCTURE is self-consistent (charming=False rows must show all downstream stages as untouched placeholders, with the correct stage label) and (c) checks charming-classification does not contradict itself for identical (m,ab(f)) pairs across the receipt. observations: Window CONSTRUCTION cost (quotient + joint-image + M-block-projection hom + Kernel + free-group epimorphism + DerivedSubgroup) is CHEAP and roughly degree-insensitive in the tested range (19-34ms even at degree=144): the earlier full-4265-row LINS-2000 sweep's 251.6ms/row average (search/certs/drophunt_calibration_v1_20260829.json calibration_c) already covers most of this cost at larger degree, and this pass's construction times are consistent with or cheaper than that baseline.

Per-candidate PREDICATE EVALUATION cost (PreImagesRepresentative + hexagon word evaluation + onto group-order check) is the dominant cost, roughly 150-850ms/candidate on the FIRST evaluation of a window, with substantial variance; a representative working estimate is ~150-300ms/candidate.

The SECOND seed evaluated on an ALREADY-BUILT window (row71 after row36) is dramatically cheaper (1-8ms total, not per-candidate) -- GAP appears to cache/reuse internal Schreier-tree-style data structures from the first PreImagesRepresentative/group-order call on the same window. This means Mode B (row71) piggy-backed on an already-swept Mode A window is essentially free; it is NOT free as a first, standalone evaluation.
Sample size is small (6 windows, F3 in {2,3,3,3,4,9}); extrapolation confidence is MODERATE, not high.

venue_recommendation.verdict: GHA recommended for a full 358-window row36-mode sweep; LOCAL is feasible ONLY as multiple checkpointed chunks.
venue_recommendation.reasoning: Estimated total 44-87 minutes (best estimate ~58 minutes) for a single unbroken row36-mode sweep of all 358 fib<=100 windows exceeds the house 10-minute local-chunk discipline by 4-9x. Per-window cost is small enough (0.5-2s typical, with occasional larger windows) that natural checkpoint boundaries exist every 20-40 windows for a 10-minute local chunk if local execution is preferred instead.
options: (a) GHA, single run, with falsifier preflight per house lane discipline (arranged by coordinator, not this implementer) -- straightforward, matches the venue already used for the LINS index/joint-image sweep in the prior calibration pass.

(b) Local, checkpoint/resume across an estimated 5-9 chunks of ~10 minutes each (~20-70 windows/chunk depending on their individual F3), writing partial receipts and a resumable cursor file between chunks -- feasible but more operational overhead than (a).

deviations_and_open_questions: (1) Charming's derived-subgroup-membership sub-check is not independently re-derived end-to-end by the checker (see checker.scope_limitation above) -- a genuine algorithmic gap given the standard-library-only constraint, not a shortcut taken for convenience.

(2) The 6-window calibration table reuses PRE-EXISTING independent producer/checker pairs (built 2026-08-23/24, before this task and before ruling 1720) rather than re-deriving all 6 with the NEW general system built in this pass, because 5 of the 6 named windows are bespoke constructions (K1 itself, K_Q, K_H, PGammaL(2,8), and the compound K2=K1 cap L3) outside the K=M cap L single-LINS-row scope that this pass's new general producer/checker targets. This is flagged for 司令塔 confirmation that reuse is acceptable here, same category as prior passes' reuse-vs-recompute flags.

(3) LINS-48B's raw fibre count and a dedicated cross-checked artifact were not relocated within this pass's time budget; only a terse campaign-status marker citation (valid=2) is reported for that one row of the calibration table.

(4) Cost/venue estimate is extrapolated from only 6 test windows (all with F3<=9); the 358-window set's actual per-window cost distribution (especially for its higher-fib members, up to fib=100) has not been directly measured and could deviate from this extrapolation.

(5) Two implementation bugs were caught and fixed mid-pass (checker's short-circuit-blind hexagon comparison; mutant #10's no-op base window) -- see mandatory_mutant_tests.self_correction_note. Reported transparently, not smoothed over.
